entities.title: GString
entities.summary: The string class the author wrote at OZ between 1998 and 2002 to end the Great String War; first called the God-String, which quickly got shortened. Its source is gone.
notToBeConfusedWith: GLib's GString, which existed at the same time and has nothing to do with it
The headers in src/gstring, which are a 2026 reconstruction of what it might have looked like

entities.title: The Great String War
entities.summary: The argument in OZ's large development team over which string class was best, with no consensus, no policy and no authority to settle it; GString ended it by making it not matter. Also the title of the series.

entities.title: Faction
entities.summary: A group of programmers at OZ loyal to one string class (Rogue Wave's RWCString, MFC's CString, std::string, the C library, Java's String or Perl), whose favourite methods GString had to offer to win its buy-in.

entities.title: OZ
entities.summary: Where GString was written, on iPulse, between 1998 and 2002.

entities.title: iPulse
entities.summary: The system at OZ whose RPC layer, which also did most of its code generation, needed GString.
